title: Console docs: Hosted canary rollouts GA (concepts, workflow, API, troubleshooting)
author: Wei Chen
description: Summary: This PR refreshes and GA-izes our documentation for Hosted canary rollouts in Redwood Console. It consolidates beta-era notes into a single GA narrative, adds a step-by-step UI walkthrough (wizard + rollout details view), documents the relevant API surfaces at a conceptual level (with request/response snippets), and adds troubleshooting guidance aligned with the current orchestrator + policy guardrails + auto-stop behavior. Motivation: Support and design partners repeatedly asked for a single source-of-truth doc that explains (1) what a Hosted canary rollout is, (2) how percentage splits behave, (3) what guardrails/approvals exist, (4) what happens on SLO breach / auto-pause / rollback, and (5) how to debug split mismatches and “stuck” steps. This PR is intended to be the doc companion to the Hosted canary workflow GA effort. What’s included: (1) New docs page: “Hosted canary rollouts (GA)” covering core concepts (baseline vs canary, cohorting, step schedule, soak time, stop conditions), limitations, and FAQs; (2) Console walkthrough: Create rollout → Review & validate → Start → Progress step → Pause/Resume → Rollback, with screenshots callouts and copy consistent with the wizard; (3) Guardrails and approvals: explains max step size / minimum soak time / approval gates at a user-facing level, with examples of policy validation errors; (4) Observability: how to interpret baseline vs canary cohort metrics (latency p50/p95, error rate, timeouts) and how auto-stop decisions are made; (5) Troubleshooting: common issues (split mismatch, unexpected auto-pause, rollout cannot progress due to soak/approval) and what to collect for support (rollout_id, route, region, timestamps, activity log events); (6) Security/governance notes: audit log event types and what fields customers can expect to see; (7) Updated docs navigation + redirects from the beta page. Not included: Dedicated/Private rollout parity docs, automated quality-gate setup, and deep policy language reference (those remain follow-ups / internal docs). Screenshots: redacted tenant names + routes; updated to current Console build as of 2025-03-26. Testing: link checker, docs build, and snippet lint pass. Rollout: will publish with Console GA announcement; support macros will link to the troubleshooting section; release notes draft updated separately.
commits: docs(console/rollouts): add GA concepts page for Hosted canary rollouts
docs(console/rollouts): add wizard walkthrough + rollout details timeline section
docs(api): document rollout-related fields and query parameters (Hosted only)
docs(troubleshooting): add playbook for auto-pause/rollback + split mismatch
docs(nav): add sidebar entries + redirect beta canary docs to GA page
chore: screenshot refresh + alt text + copy alignment with Console strings
review_conversation: Elliot Price (review): The concepts page looks solid. Two nits: (1) we should be explicit that cohorting is deterministic but not guaranteed to be per end-user unless they provide a stable key; (2) “auto-rollback” vs “auto-pause” terminology is inconsistent across sections. Also, can we add a short “What data do we log?” callout in troubleshooting to reduce back-and-forth with support? Wei Chen (author): Updated the cohorting section to call out the default stickiness key (request hash inputs) and added guidance for providing a stable user/session identifier (when available) to get more consistent end-user experience. Also normalized language to “auto-stop” with outcomes “auto-pause” or “auto-rollback” depending on policy. Added a “Collect this for support” block with rollout_id, route, region, and timestamps + activity log export. Marissa Cole (review): The UI walkthrough matches the wizard flow, but the warning callouts should match current copy (esp. the rollback confirmation). Also can we mention where approvals show up (timeline vs modal) to set expectations? Wei Chen (author): Synced warning copy and updated screenshots from latest build. Added a note in the Approvals section: approval requests appear as a gated action in the step progression dialog and are recorded in the rollout activity timeline with actor + timestamp. Dylan Brooks (review): API page: please avoid implying these endpoints are public GA for everyone; we have tenant gating during staged rollout. Suggest phrasing: “available for eligible tenants; see enablement” and link to Console availability note. Also add a small disclaimer about region behavior (split is applied per-request in region after smart routing). Wei Chen (author): Updated wording to “available for eligible tenants” and added an Availability block. Added a “How splits are applied” note: route selection happens first, then canary split is enforced in the selected region using deterministic cohorting. Sean Gallagher (review): Troubleshooting: add guidance for interpreting short-term latency spikes (warm cache / cold start) and advise minimum soak times before escalating. Also include the default stop-condition signals we page on (5xx, timeouts, p95 regression) without giving exact thresholds (those vary). Wei Chen (author): Added a “Before you rollback” subsection describing warm-up effects and suggesting a minimum observation window aligned with configured soak time. Added a list of common stop-condition signals without embedding exact thresholds. Marcus Lin (review): Audit logging section: please state that audit log event fields vary by plan/retention and include an example event payload, but redact tenant IDs. Also make sure we don’t claim SIEM export in GA docs unless it’s actually enabled for Hosted tenants. Wei Chen (author): Added a redacted example event and adjusted wording to “audit logs can be exported via supported integrations where enabled” (no blanket SIEM claim). Also added a note about retention depending on plan.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Elliot Price. Post-merge: publish job scheduled with Console GA announcement bundle.
release_notes: Docs: Added GA documentation for Hosted canary rollouts including concepts, Console walkthrough, baseline vs canary metrics interpretation, audit logging overview, and troubleshooting for auto-pause/rollback and split mismatch scenarios.
